title: Automated image analysis method for oil-release test of lipid-based materials
author: Valoppi, Lassila, et al.
materials: and the steps of the analysis (Script #

steps.title: Assemble imaging platform
steps.instruction: Place a tripod (height 21.5 cm, circular opening diameter 12.1 cm) on a stable surface, attach a full‑HD digital webcam (Lenovo Essential) to an optical table so the camera aperture is perpendicular to the table, and position a paper cylinder (height 75 cm, diameter 20 cm, wall thickness 0.4 cm, total folded thickness 1.2 cm) around the opening to provide a uniform light background.

substeps.instruction: Verify that the portion of the camera view containing the filter paper is optically flat (checked with graph paper).
Ensure the sample mass will stay below 4 g to avoid bending the filter paper.

steps.title: Prepare sample and filter paper
steps.instruction: Cut a 10 % monoglyceride‑based oleogel into cylinders (diameter 20 mm, height 7–10 mm, mass 3.25 ± 0.5 g) using a metallic cylindrical shaper, place each cylinder on a Whatman filter‑paper #2 disk (pore 8 µm, thickness 190 µm, diameter 15 cm), and then set the disk on the tripod.

steps.title: Set lighting and environment
steps.instruction: Position a commercial neon‑tube light 1 m above the setup, keep its intensity constant throughout the experiment, and perform the test at room temperature 22 ± 1 °C (temperature should be controlled for reproducibility).

steps.title: Configure and start image capture
steps.instruction: Install YawCam v.0.7.0 on a laptop, set the capture interval to every 10 min, start the software, and begin automatic acquisition. The distance from the camera lens to the bottom of the filter paper must be 15 cm. Capture images for the desired total duration (e.g., 33 h).

substeps.instruction: Images are saved in a temporary Windows folder; do not move them until acquisition is finished.

steps.title: Transfer captured images
steps.instruction: After the acquisition ends, copy the image files from the temporary folder to a permanent destination folder for later analysis.

steps.title: Edit ImageJ macro paths
steps.instruction: Download the two ImageJ macro files (Image Conversion for Oil Release Analysis.ijm and Calculation Oil Release Analysis.ijm), open each in ImageJ via Plugins → Macros → Edit…, replace the placeholder folder paths with the actual full paths on your computer (use forward slashes “/” and end each path with a trailing slash).

steps.title: Convert and downscale images (Script #1)
steps.instruction: Run the first macro to process all images in the input folder:

substeps.instruction: The macro opens each image, runs "8-bit", scales it to 50 % (x=0.5 y=0.5 width=960 height=540 interpolation=Bilinear average create), saves it as a JPEG in the output folder, and closes the image.
If the camera is not full‑HD, fewer than 20–30 images are used, or the computer is powerful enough, the scaling command can be removed or commented out (prepend //).

steps.title: Analyze oil‑stain area (Script #2)
steps.instruction: Run the second macro on the converted images to obtain the oil‑stain area:

substeps.instruction: Set the scale using a reference (distance=416 pixels, known=12.1 cm, pixel=1, unit=cm, global).
Enhance contrast with saturated=0.35 and apply the LUT.
Create an oval region of interest that matches the tripod opening (default makeOval(265,46,431,432); adjust coordinates if needed).
Set background color to black (0,0,0) and run "Clear Outside" to mask everything outside the ROI.
Apply automatic threshold (Default dark) and then set the lower threshold to 170 and upper to 255.
Enable "BlackBackground" option, convert the image to a mask, and run "Analyze Particles..." with size=0.005‑Infinity and summarize the results.
Close the image (or comment out the close() command to keep images open for visual inspection).
